Subject: Discovery Recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Health)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and agreed on from the discovery call:

Pain points / priorities:
- Handling PII in prompts and model outputs (PHI-sensitive fields); must ensure redaction before long-term storage.
- Auditability: need detailed request/response audit logs for compliance reviews and incident investigation.
- Retention policy: different retention requirements by data class (short-term logs ~90 days, some records up to 7 years).
- Encryption & isolation: data at rest must be encrypted; preference for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Minimal bucket/host access: logs should be exportable to Acme-managed storage.

Current stack we heard: AWS (EKS), customers interact through internal API gateway, ingestion pipeline uses S3, Splunk for aggregated logs.

Success criteria for pilot:
1) Clear PII redaction or mutation options before persistent logs.
2) Configurable retention per log class and ability to export raw/aggregated logs to Acme S3.
3) Audit log granularity to show request id, timestamp, model used, route, and redaction flag.
4) Proof of controls: SOC2 attestation + implementation notes.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- I will share this recap + attachments: discovery_notes.pdf and Redwood SOC2_Attestation.pdf (attached). (Marissa) — today
- Technical deep-dive with Rishi & Dev to cover redaction approaches and export hooks (Rishi / Dev) — propose Mon/Tue next week; please confirm availability
- Share a short matrix of redaction options + retention configs for legal/infosec (Rishi) — by end of next week

Attachments: discovery_notes.pdf (call notes), SOC2_Attestation.pdf

If I missed anything or you want the summary adjusted, please let me know. Otherwise I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive for next week and loop in the engineering contacts.

Thanks,

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the questions — happy to clarify from a technical standpoint. Short answers first, details below.

- Export: We support export to customer S3 (push) and provide a fluentd/syslog-compatible exporter for Splunk; export can be pushed in near real-time or batched.
- Redaction: Redwood supports multiple modes: full redaction (remove PII tokens from persisted logs), token hashing (store irreversible hash + token metadata), and pseudonymization (consistent id map). Redaction can be configured per route or per data-class. See attached redaction_requirements.xlsx for mapping examples.
- KMS: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS keys for any persisted artifacts we export to S3. For hosted logs, we can encrypt at rest with our keys but offer an option to route logs to your S3 (preferred for compliance).

More specifics:
1) Audit log fields: request_id, timestamp (ISO8601, UTC), route/model, user_agent, obfuscated_user_id, redaction_profile_used, redaction_flag (true/false), token_count, latency_ms.
2) Retention controls: retention policies are configurable per-log-type in the Console or via API. Typical pilot config: ephemeral request traces (7 days), operational logs (90 days), exportable full audit logs (retained according to customer S3 lifecycle rules).
3) Redaction timing: redaction can be applied before any data is persisted (server-side), and we provide a preview mode so you can validate what will be kept vs removed.
4) Access & SOC2 items: our SOC2 covers logical access controls, encryption in transit, and logging of admin changes; attached is the attestation. For additional evidence we can provide a scoped list of controls and a point-in-time evidence package under an NDA.

Action items I’ll take after this thread:
- Share redaction matrix (attached: redaction_requirements.xlsx)
- Draft a pilot config (retention + export settings) and a short runbook for export to Acme S3 (Dev will help)

If you’re good with Mon 3/23 10:00–11:30 PT, I’ll send a calendar invite with a Teams link and a proposed agenda (redaction demo, retention API, export runbook).

Thanks,
